excerpt: I was remembering scenes, not facts … I was recalling scenes … that is … I could clearly recall a scene of me at the beach in New London with my family as a child. But the feeling was that the scene was not my memory. As if I was looking at a photo of someone else’s vacation. Note that these memories were substantiated by third parties as valid renditions of events that actually transpired in R.B.’s life.
overview: The beach recollection matters because it satisfies the article's criteria for episodic recall: a scene located in time and space, involving R.B., and corroborated as autobiographical. Its lack of ownership directly supports the dissociation rather than merely showing semantic relearning.
title: Beach Scene Without Ownership
